description: One low frequency oscillator with a shape that morphs continuously, and a modulation input for each of its three controls.

params.text: How much the FQ jack moves the rate. With nothing patched into FQ this knob is a fine tune on the rate instead.
Morphs the shape through triangle, sine, rounded square and square.
How much the WF jack moves the shape.
Skews the shape, moving the peak towards one end of the cycle or the other.
How much the SYM jack moves that skew.
Sets the rate range: up is the fastest, middle is the range meant for one-volt-per-octave control, down is the slowest.

inputs.text: Moves the skew, by as much as the MOD knob beside SYM allows.
Moves the shape, by as much as the MOD knob beside WF allows.
A clock for the oscillator: a rising edge restarts its cycle, and the FQ knob is then read as a division of that clock.
Moves the rate, by as much as the MOD knob beside FQ allows.
Holds the output at its present value while this is low, and lets the oscillator run while it is high.
Returns the oscillator to the start of its cycle on each rising edge.

outputs.text: The oscillator with its phase turned round half a cycle.

notes: Set Rack's sample rate to 96kHz before using this module. At any other rate it runs at the wrong speed, and a red bar appears across the bottom of the panel saying so.
An unpatched modulation CV jack does not read 0V: the firmware drives it from an internal chaotic generator, so a MOD knob turned up with nothing patched lets a wandering voltage through.
